findings.reason: Hindi CLDR `one` covers 0 and 1 (hi style guide: "0 फ़ाइल" is singular), so the verb must agree with the shown count; the fixed हैं renders "कुल 1 चैट में से 1 दिखाई जा रही हैं" for the common one-chat state, which a native reader reads as wrong, and the same at 0. A plural on the already-present `shown` argument fixes only the 0/1 arm and leaves 2+ unchanged; rendered above.

verdict: clean-with-findings — 49/49 values read, 0 blocker, 0 major, 1 minor (HI-FINAL-01, non-gating); the six delta values and the carried keys match English and the sidecar roles, and the plural arms render correctly at 0/1/2/6/7/1000.

outside_scope_observations.observation: The English source attaches a fixed plural noun to a bare total, so total=1 renders "Showing 1 of 1 chats" (and "Showing 1 match of 1 chats"). fr/es/vi/ru avoid a finite verb; hi and ur use one, which is why hi exposes the 0/1 agreement gap recorded as HI-FINAL-01. English-side, non-gating for hi.

English uses `#`, so 1000 renders "1,000 chats in this group"; every translated locale including hi suppresses grouping with ::group-off. House-wide divergence, not a hi defect; recorded so a rendered check knows what to expect (hi renders "इस समूह में 1000 चैट").

chat-sidebar.tsx joins the names with an English " and " before passing them as {list}, so a Hindi sentence shows "Alpha and Beta". The code comment states this as a stated ICU limit, not an oversight; it is not a catalogue value and cannot be fixed in the hi file. The =0 arm is unreachable at this call site (availableBuiltins.length > 0 gates it).
